sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Bayonne?
sections.html:
Bayonne is a dense Hudson County city, with 74,744 residents on a peninsula that has 5.82 square miles of land. A sale there involves a resale certificate through the city, a deed recorded by the Hudson County Register, and for many sellers a look at short-term rental and rent control rules.

This page covers the local numbers, the city steps and the county and state filings, so you can decide whether to list, sell on your own or accept an as-is cash purchase.

sections.h2: What does Bayonne look like on paper?
sections.html:
Bayonne sits on Bergen Neck, a peninsula bounded by Newark Bay, the Kill Van Kull and Upper New York Bay, and it borders Jersey City to the north. The 2020 census counted 71,686 people, up 13.7% from 63,024 in 2010, and the Census Bureau estimates 74,744 for mid-2025.

With about 36% of homes owner-occupied, two- and three-family houses and condos are a large part of the market, and landlords are common sellers. The median home value of $460,100 also sets the price range most buyers will compare against.

sections.h2: How does Bayonne's history and economy affect sellers?
sections.html:
Bayonne was set off as a township in 1861 and reincorporated as a city in 1869, uniting Bergen Point, Constable Hook, Centreville, Pamrapo and Saltersville. Manufacturing, distribution and maritime work still anchor the economy, and part of the Port of New York and New Jersey lies in the city at Port Jersey.

The Cape Liberty Cruise Port sits at the end of the peninsula on the former Military Ocean Terminal, where The Peninsula at Bayonne Harbor now has housing and businesses. Bayonne Medical Center anchors the Broadway shopping district and is the city's largest employer, with more than 1,200 employees. Census retail sales for 2022 reached about $849 million, and transportation and warehousing receipts topped $520 million.

sections.h2: Which roads, rail and schools shape Bayonne home values?
sections.html:
Commuters rely on the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail, which has four Bayonne stops at 45th Street, 34th Street, 22nd Street and 8th Street, and on the Newark Bay Extension of the New Jersey Turnpike (Interstate 78). The Bayonne Bridge, which opened in 1931 and was raised between 2013 and 2019, links the city to Staten Island.

The Bayonne School District serves pre-kindergarten through twelfth grade with 13 schools and 10,059 students in 2020-21, according to Wikipedia. Parks matter to buyers too, including the Hackensack RiverWalk at Collins Park and the Stephen R. Gregg Hudson County Park.

  • The light rail connects Bayonne with Jersey City and its neighbors, and with PATH stations and ferry terminals.
  • The Route 440 retail corridor includes Bayonne Crossing.
  • Average travel time to work is 33.7 minutes, so listings near transit tend to note it.

sections.h2: What resale certificate does Bayonne require?
sections.html:
Bayonne requires a resale certificate whenever a building is sold, and a May 2026 city notice moved that process to the Fire Prevention Bureau at City Hall. Applicants pick up the application from the Fire Prevention office, complete the inspection, and the Fire Department issues the certificate for the sale.

This replaced an earlier arrangement. On October 1, 2025, the Building Department stopped issuing Continuing Certificates of Occupancy and began issuing Resale Certificates for one-family, two-family and multi-family dwellings and commercial buildings. The city said at the time that only the name changed and that the application was shorter. Because the office handling it moved again in 2026, call the Fire Prevention Bureau before you schedule closing. The September 2025 notice listed Building Department lines at 201-858-6334 and 201-858-6073 for certificate questions, which remain useful for permit history on the property.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Bayonne house that has been a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Yes, but the city's short-term rental ordinance sets rules that a buyer will want proof of. Under Chapter 33, a short-term rental is occupancy of 60 consecutive days or fewer, and only a property owner can hold the license.

  • Applications go through the city's Spatial Data Logic online portal.
  • Fire safety, building and zoning inspections come first, and the city says a license follows within 30 calendar days of satisfactory inspections.
  • Applicants show no outstanding taxes or water and sewer charges, prior code violations abated and open construction permits closed.
  • A zoning determination letter costs $50 and is requested from the zoning officer at City Hall.
  • A tenant cannot hold the license.

The city website also lists a Rent Control board and a Small Landlord Emergency Grant Program page. If your building has tenants, ask the Planning, Zoning and Development office whether rent control covers it.

sections.h2: Who handles the deed and the state filings in Bayonne?
sections.html:
Bayonne is in Hudson County, so the deed is recorded by the Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which lists a phone number of 201-395-4760 on the county directory. Sellers pay the state realty transfer fee. For sales over $350,000, the schedule starts at $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000 and rises to $4.80 per $500 between $200,000 and $550,000.

If you own a Bayonne house but live outside New Jersey, the state requires a GIT/REP form with the deed. Nonresident sellers prepay the larger of 10.75% of their gain or 2% of the deed consideration, so a landlord with a rental in Bayonne should ask the closing agent to calculate the payment before the day of settlement.

sections.h2: Should I list, sell myself, or take a cash offer in Bayonne?
sections.html:
Compare the three on time, cost and risk, using written numbers from each buyer or agent. A cash purchase as-is can avoid repair work and showings, while a listing may reach more buyers on a $460,100 median market.

Whichever way you go, schedule the resale inspection early, since the certificate gates the closing. Mortgage payoff, tax bills and any water and sewer balance come off the proceeds at settlement, and the city lists online payment pages for taxes and water and sewer so you can pull current balances. The same site links an Emergency Rescue Mortgage Assistance page, which is worth reading if missed payments are pushing you to sell.

faqs.q: What is the Bayonne resale certificate?
faqs.a: It is the certificate the city requires whenever a building is sold. As of the city's May 2026 notice, the Fire Prevention Bureau at City Hall issues it after an inspection.

faqs.q: Did Bayonne get rid of the continuing certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Department replaced the CCO with a Resale Certificate on October 1, 2025, and the city described the change as a rename with a shorter application.

faqs.q: Where is a Bayonne deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records it. The county directory lists that office at 201-395-4760.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bayonne property that I rent short term?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Chapter 33 ordinance limits short-term rentals to 60 days or fewer and requires an owner license with inspections, so confirm your license status before you sign a contract.

faqs.q: Do out-of-state owners owe tax when selling in Bayonne?
faqs.a: They owe a prepayment with the GIT/REP form. The minimum is 2% of the consideration shown on the deed, and the state formula can produce a higher amount based on the gain.
